text:
Ben Rivera: Heads-up: pushing canary for runtime change rtx-opt-3 to hosted and dedicated tonight. Observed a small p95 regression on long-context workloads in local perf tests. Posting raw numbers below, need quick gate decision.

release-bot: Canary rtx-opt-3 started on pool canary-042 (deploy id: canary-20260317-42) :rocket:

Ben Rivera: Local benchmark (8k tokens, batch=1) — baseline (main @ v1.14.0):
```
p50: 98ms
p90: 210ms
p95: 260ms
p99: 410ms
```
Ben Rivera: With rtx-opt-3 on same infra:
```
p50: 92ms
p90: 220ms
p95: 305ms  <-- regression
p99: 420ms
```
Ben Rivera: The throughput numbers look fine; this seems latency tail for long contexts. Not sure if it's caused by KV cache handling changes or kernel selection path.

Alice Cho: Oof, p95 +45ms is non-trivial for some latency SLOs. Do we see this on shorter contexts?

Ben Rivera: Short contexts (<=512): no regression; actually slight improvement. So it's specific to long sequences.

Diego Morales: Possibly related to the new attention packing heuristic. Can you run the flame profiler on the failing request? Use `perf-collect --req <req_id> --duration 30s` from eng-runtime tools.

Ben Rivera: Running now against canary request id 20260317-rtx-891. Output snippet:
```
[flame] top frames: kv_cache_handler::merge_async (40%)
           attention_kernel::dispatch (25%)
           io_scheduler::wait (15%)
```
Ben Rivera: KV cache merge looks heavy. Might be contention on small GPU mem copies.

Cara Patel: Suggest we gate the canary rollout—hold expanding to more hosts. Product/PM sign-off required before wider rollout. @Erin Zhang can you weigh in on user impact?

Erin Zhang: If p95 regressed for some customers using long-context chains (e.g., developer tools, code assistants), it could be user-visible in sessions. Recommend hold unless we can pinpoint and mitigate within next 6 hours.

Alice Cho: Quick mitigation we can try: enable `--kv-merge-eager=false` flag in canary to switch back to incremental merge strategy. It's safe to toggle at runtime for canary pool. Whoever can flip it, please do and re-run perf.

Ben Rivera: I can toggle it on canary-042. Doing `infractl canary config set canary-042 --set runtime.kv_merge_eager=false` now.

release-bot: Config update applied to canary-042 by Ben Rivera.

Ben Rivera: Re-ran benchmark after flag change:
```
p50: 95ms
p90: 215ms
p95: 265ms  <-- back to near baseline
p99: 415ms
```
Ben Rivera: Looks much better.

Diego Morales: That aligns with the flame profile; eager merge path introduced larger copies. We should add a microbenchmark for merge path and a unit perf test in CI to prevent regressions. I'll open a small PR with a microbenchmark harness.

Alice Cho: Agreed. For rollout decision: keep canary paused, but we can proceed with gradual rollout once we've got the config default changed or the eager merge fixed. Also add a canary gate to check `p95_long_context_delta <= 30ms` against baseline.

Cara Patel: I'll hold the rollout and update the release notes: "canary paused due to long-context p95 regression; mitigation toggled."

Erin Zhang: Product approval: conditional. Approve expanding to +10% once the `kv_merge_eager=false` config is the default for canary and perf dashboards show p95 within threshold for 30 minutes.

Ben Rivera: Action items: (1) Diego PR for microbenchmark + CI perf test (assigned Diego). (2) Engineering to investigate optimizing merge path (Alice + Ben). (3) Ops to keep canary paused and monitor metrics (Cara). (4) Product to confirm after 30m (Erin). I'll keep posting perf snapshots here.

release-bot: Canary canary-042 metrics: https://console.redwood.example/canary-042/metrics (auto-updates)

Diego Morales: PR opened: https://git.redwood/rtx/merge-profiles/pull/314 — adds merge microbenchmark and CI check.

Alice Cho: Starting deeper profiling now. If we find a kernel-level fix we might flip `kv_merge_eager` back on at canary and re-evaluate.

Cara Patel: Logging action: scheduled rollback window if regression reappears. If p95 delta > 40ms for 3 consecutive 5m buckets, automatic rollback to main will trigger.

Ben Rivera: Thanks all. For traceability: marking thread for release notes and postmortem if we hit rollback. Will update within 30m.

Erin Zhang: Thanks — appreciate the quick reaction. :thumbsup:
